Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to lock Ceres-7B quant variant for staged rollout + compat checks

Hi team,

Product is asking to pin the new Ceres-7B quantized variant (ceres-7b-quant-v2) as a candidate for our beta program with a staged rollout. Before we flip any routing or pin policies I need engineering and safety to confirm compatibility and any caveats that would block a targeted rollout. High-level asks: 

- Dev: run a compat check with our serving runtime (kernel list, memory/kv behavior, latency delta vs current gated variants). Please populate compat-matrix.csv with failing ops and perf deltas.
- Neha/Infra: estimate required pool sizes for Dedicated vs hosted (cost delta estimate for 100 rps steady + spikes).
- Markus/Safety: quick triage for output safety regressions or known failure modes for the quant path; if you need eval prompts, I attached an initial prompt set.

Target timeline: quick triage within 48h, deeper tests by EOD Thu (7/23). If anything blocks rollout we should document explicit fallback variants and rollout kill-switch.

Attachments: ceres-v2-metadata.json (from vendor).

Thanks — happy to sync if useful.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
messages_2:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to lock Ceres-7B quant variant for staged rollout + compat checks

Stephanie —

Thanks, I kicked off a quick smoke pass on the runtime. Early findings (very preliminary):

- Binary format: variant uses 4-bit grouped quant + custom fused attention kernel. Loading on a standard A10 instance works but we see increased kernel fallbacks on 80-token contexts.
- KV cache behavior: there is a minor mismatch in KV layout for the fused-attn path that forces an extra copy on warmup; adds ~8–14ms per request at 32 tokens on our baseline config.
- Memory: peak GPU memory is ~1.1x vs our current gated 7B quant; CPU-side memory looks fine.

I created compat-matrix.csv in the Drive folder with flagged ops and a short repro. I also attached a small trace (referenced in the drive link) — vendor artifact seems to call aten::fused_attn_v2 which our current kernel set maps to a fallback.

Immediate ask: can vendor provide an alternative kernel or a mapping shim? Without it we can still serve but we'll need to advertise a slightly higher p95.

I'll schedule a 30-min test slot Wed morning to run a batched-throughput experiment and include Neha for capacity numbers.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Runtime
Redwood Inference
messages_3:
From: Ceres AI <ceres-ai@vendor.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:53:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to lock Ceres-7B quant variant for staged rollout + compat checks

Hi Dev and Stephanie,

Thanks for the heads-up and the trace. We reproduced the fallback behavior on our side: the fused_attn_v2 op was an experimental kernel intended to reduce memory traffic but it assumes a grouped-4 bit layout that differs slightly from the canonical layout.

Options we can offer this week:
1) Provide a compatibility shim (python/cpp) that rewrites the op to a supported fused_attn form. This adds ~6ms overhead but removes the extra copy.
2) Export an alternate build of the model using the canonical grouping (ceres-7b-quant-v2-canonical) — slightly larger on disk but cleaner runtime behavior.

We attached ceres-v2-metadata.json and a short note on the canonical export tradeoffs. If you choose shim route we can provide a patch and short integration test by EOD Thu.

Let us know which path you prefer. We are also open to a short sync to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
—Jaya Rao
Platform Integrations Lead
Ceres AI

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to lock Ceres-7B quant variant for staged rollout + compat checks

Quick safety note — thanks for the context. I reviewed the initial eval prompts in the Drive folder. Preliminary concerns:

- Quantization artifacts observed in small-sample evaluations: hallucination modes increase subtly on instruction-following prompts, primarily when the model is in the fused-attn codepath. Not catastrophic but measurable.
- We should gate any wide rollout on a targeted eval battery (1000 prompts) and hold off on pinning to the entire product until we see regression < 1.5% vs baseline on our quality metric.

Proposal: allow a narrow beta (5% of traffic) routed to ceres-7b-quant-v2-canonical (if vendor can produce canonical) OR ceres-7b-quant-v2+shim with feature flagging. During the beta, collect prompt-level QA traces and failover to the current stable 7B-quant if regression spike detected.

I can own the eval run if you folks can provide the canonical build or the shim patch by Thu EOD.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Safety & Trust
Redwood Inference
